title: Ringed pro-etale open-closed localization
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], and use $i^{-1}A,j^{-1}A$ on $Z,U$. The inverse images and direct images are those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and $j_!$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]: the presheaf value at $V\to X$ is the given module evaluated at $V\to U$ if this factorization exists, and is zero otherwise. The localization of sites is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], with their induced module actions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The module functor $j_!$ is left adjoint to $j^{-1}$. These functors satisfy $i^{-1}i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$, $j^{-1}j_!\cong\operatorname{id}$, $j^{-1}i_*=0$, and $i^{-1}j_!=0$. The functors $j_!$ and $i_*$ are exact. For every $A$-module sheaf $M$ the counit and unit give a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] $0\to j_!j^{-1}M\to M\to i_*i^{-1}M\to0$. If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $i_*$ commutes with small filtered colimits of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 09BM, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; Tag 09AG, lemma-jshriek-zero. Module actions and filtered-colimit clause are deductions: use Tag 0738, sites-lemma-directed-colimits-sections on qcqs V and V times_X Z. Extension-by-zero adjunction and exactness: Tag 03DI, sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero.; Tag 03DJ, sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero-exact (exactness of module extension by zero).

proof.text: Construct the closed module adjunction by transporting the model-site pullback/pushforward adjunction through the actual AsSmall module equivalences. Construct the open extension/restriction adjunction by the explicit direct-sum hom equivalence and module sheafification. Prove the open unit is invertible: the extension presheaf restricted to the slice is naturally isomorphic to the original sheaf by the singleton summand map. Sheafification commutes with slice restriction, so the restriction of its unit is invertible. The actual extension unit is the composite of this map with the singleton inclusion, so it is invertible after forgetting to abelian presheaves, and hence in modules. Obtain q and its natural comparison from the open-comparison step; obtain the invertible closed counit from the closed-counit step.

Over U, every closed fibre is empty because the images are complementary. The empty sieve covers that object, so every module sheaf has zero sections there. This proves J R=0. The two adjunction hom equivalences then turn endomorphisms of i^* j!G into maps from G to J R(i^*j!G), a zero object; identity equals zero, proving i^* j!G=0. No localization sequence is needed for this second vanishing.

Prove extension-presheaf finite-limit preservation by evaluation: the factorization index is empty or a singleton by monicity. Its value functor is respectively zero or slice evaluation. Forgetting to abelian presheaves reflects finite limits. Exact module sheafification gives finite-limit preservation of j!, while its adjunction gives colimit preservation. Right adjointness gives finite-limit preservation of i*.

Use the local short-exact-sequence step. The open comparison and immersion inverse-image preservation give exactness of J; immersion preservation also gives exactness of i^*. The sequence detects zero objects from both restrictions. For an epimorphism f on Z, the cokernel of R(f) has zero i^* restriction by the invertible counit, and zero J restriction by J R=0. It is therefore zero. Thus R preserves epis; a right adjoint between these abelian categories preserving epis preserves homology and finite colimits.
Apply the proved module filtered-colimit transfer to the concrete direct-image functor under the qcqs assumptions.
